title: Crostini misti
subtitle: Assorted Italian toasts with four toppings
excerpt: Small toasted bread rounds topped with a selection of Italian antipasto spreads and toppings: chicken liver pâté, whipped cannellini, roasted cherry tomatoes, and gorgonzola with walnut. Served as a mixed antipasto platter.
sourceNotes: Crostini misti is a classic Tuscan antipasto tradition documented in Ada Boni's Il Talismano della Felicità (1929) and in Pellegrino Artusi's La Scienza in Cucina e l'Arte di Mangiar Bene (1891, public domain). Both document the Tuscan tradition of toasted bread rounds with various savory toppings as a precursor to the meal.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: All four toppings can be made up to 2 days ahead and refrigerated. Toast the bread and assemble within 30 minutes of serving.

content.text: Crostini misti is not one recipe but four, arranged together on a platter. Each topping is simple; the combination is the point. A good antipasto table has variety: something rich, something acidic, something herby, something sharp. This selection covers those bases and can be adjusted depending on what you have and what your guests eat.

items.prepNote: or a baguette, sliced into 1 cm rounds

content.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Arrange the bread rounds on a baking tray. Brush both sides lightly with olive oil. Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until golden and crisp. Leave to cool on the tray.

Chicken liver: melt 20 g butter in a frying pan over high heat. Add the shallots and cook for 3 minutes. Add the livers and sage, season, and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until just cooked through but still slightly pink inside. Add the wine and reduce for 1 minute. Transfer to a food processor and pulse to a rough pâté with the remaining butter. Taste and season.

Cannellini: drain and rinse the beans. Warm the olive oil in a small pan with the garlic and rosemary for 2 minutes. Discard the rosemary and garlic. Mash the beans roughly with the infused oil. Season with salt. Keep chunky rather than completely smooth.

Roasted tomato: toss the cherry tomato halves with olive oil on a baking tray. Season and roast at 200°C for 15 minutes until slightly collapsed and caramelised. Cool, then scatter with torn basil leaves before serving.
Gorgonzola and walnut: no cooking needed. Spread soft gorgonzola onto crostini at the last minute. Top with a few walnut pieces and a tiny drizzle of honey.
Spread or arrange each topping on 5 to 6 crostini per type. Arrange on a large platter and serve at room temperature.

Crostini are the antipasto of Tuscany. Florence, Siena, and the hill towns of Chianti serve them at every meal that starts with more than one dish. A rough chicken-liver pâté on toasted Tuscan bread is the local standard. The mixed version, crostini misti, allows a kitchen to show range. In an Italian household, a platter of crostini misti before Sunday lunch signals that the cook has taken care. The toppings are house-made, the bread is properly toasted, and the variety is generous.
